Receipt — Edit

The Receipt form enables you to record money coming into your business through bank accounts or cash accounts. This form documents all incoming transactions for accurate financial tracking and proper allocation to income accounts.

Types of Receipts

Receipts can be recorded for various types of incoming funds:

• Customer payments - Money received from customers paying sales invoices

• Interest income - Interest earned on bank accounts or investments

• Asset sales - Proceeds from selling fixed assets or investments

• Loans received - Funds borrowed from banks or other lenders

• Other income - Any other money coming into your business

Recording a Receipt

To record a receipt, follow these steps:

1. Select the bank or cash account where the money was received

2. Enter the date when the receipt occurred

3. Specify who made the payment using the Paid by field

4. For customer receipts, the system automatically displays outstanding invoices that can be marked as paid

5. For other receipts, allocate the amounts to appropriate income accounts

6. Add any applicable tax codes if the receipt includes taxes

Bank Reconciliation

If a receipt hasn't cleared your bank account yet, mark it as Pending. This helps with accurate bank reconciliation by distinguishing between recorded receipts and those that have actually cleared your bank. Once the receipt clears, you can update its status during the bank reconciliation process.

Advanced Features

The receipt form supports several advanced features:

• Split receipts - Allocate a single receipt across multiple income accounts

• Partial payments - Record partial payments against sales invoices

• Foreign currency - Handle receipts in different currencies with automatic exchange rate calculations

• Custom fields - Add custom information specific to your business needs

This form contains the following fields:

Date

Enter the date when you received this payment.

This date determines when the receipt is recorded in your books and which accounting period it belongs to.

For bank deposits, use the date you deposited the funds, not necessarily when the bank clears them.

Reference

Enter a reference number to uniquely identify this receipt.

Common references include receipt numbers, check numbers, bank deposit slips, or payment confirmation codes.

References help you match receipts to bank statements and locate specific transactions later.

Paid by

Select the type of payer making this payment.

Choose Customer for customer payments against sales invoices or prepayments.

Choose Supplier for refunds or credit notes from suppliers.

Choose Other for payments from non-customer/supplier sources like loans, grants, or miscellaneous income.

Received in

Select the Bank account or CashAccount that received this payment.

The selected account's balance will increase by the receipt amount.

If you haven't created the receiving account yet, set it up under Bank and Cash Accounts first.

Cleared

Select the clearing status for bank deposits.

Choose Cleared if the bank has already processed and credited your account.

Choose Pending if the deposit is made but not yet showing in your bank statement.

This status is crucial for accurate bank reconciliation and cash flow reporting.

Exchange rate

Enter the Exchange rate for converting foreign currency receipts to your Base Currency.

This rate applies when receiving payment into a foreign currency bank account.

The exchange rate determines the base currency value for financial reporting.

You can configure automatic exchange rates under Settings → Exchange Rates.

Description

Enter an optional description to provide context about this receipt.

Descriptions help identify the payment source and purpose when reviewing transactions.

Include details like payment method, customer PO numbers, or the reason for payment.

Lines

Add line items to allocate this receipt to appropriate accounts.

Each line can post to different IncomeAccounts, apply to Sales Invoices, or record SalesItems.

Use multiple lines to split a single payment across different income categories or invoices.

Lines without accounts will be automatically allocated to the oldest unpaid invoices for the selected customer.

Inventory Location

Select the Inventory Location when receiving payment for inventory items.

This determines which warehouse or location's inventory quantities will be reduced.

Only appears when you have enabled inventory locations and are receiving payment for inventory items.

Amounts are tax exclusive

Specify whether line amounts include or exclude tax.

Check this box if amounts are tax-exclusive - tax will be calculated and added to line amounts.

Leave unchecked if amounts already include tax - tax will be calculated but included in the line amount.

This setting affects the final receipt total and how tax amounts are displayed.

Fixed total

Enable fixed total to force this receipt to match a specific amount.

Useful when you need to match exact bank deposit amounts or handle rounding differences.

Any difference between line items and the fixed total will be automatically posted to SuspenseAccount.

The suspense account entry helps you investigate and correct discrepancies later.

FixedTotalAmount

Enter the exact total amount for this receipt.

Line items will be recorded as entered, but the receipt total will match this fixed amount.

Any difference is posted to SuspenseAccount, creating an audit trail for discrepancies.

Review suspense account entries regularly to identify and resolve differences.
